identity_limit: LM Studio model identifier; weights and lineage not independently verified in this review
content:
- Define denominators as auditable gold units—entities, edges, rules, blueprints per document family—and report precision/recall only over in-scope units, with N/A for absent types and explicit false-positive/false-negative counts for ownership, negation, and process exceptions.

- Add anti-gaming controls: sealed heldout families, versioned schemas, blind independent annotators, contamination checks against the three 100MB dev repos, separate fixed-harness model runs from end-to-end system runs, and a defined recovery protocol so UI/postprocessing cannot hide failures.

- Make human gold subgraphs auditable: require inter-annotator agreement thresholds, adjudication logs, source-span evidence, and negative examples; “independent” must mean annotators do not see PALO outputs or business-user edits, otherwise the gold is contaminated by the system under test.

- Ship a practical first release: 2–3 heldout document families with a fixed small corpus, one sealed gold subgraph set, one governance-fault suite, and raw per-task tables for semantic precision/recall, graph consistency, traceability, recovery, actual business-user edit time per accepted correction, and total billed cost including failures.

- Compare only by task role, not borrowed scores: HELM-style multi-metric transparency, OfficeQA document QA, DABstep data-analysis workflows, SWE-bench repo repair; do not claim parity or import current results, and make cost/edit-time denominators explicit per completed run or accepted correction.
note: Earlier attempts are retained as delivery failures, not counted as substantive independent reviews.
